constraints.variable: All valves: pneumatic leak test and proof pressure test requirements per section 4.3.1
constraints.review_reason: Qualitative compliance requirement; no directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
a. [NCPR 16] All valves shall meet pneumatic leak test and proof pressure test
requirements in accordance with section 4.3.1 in this NASA Technical Specification.

constraints.variable: Each valve lot: burst pressure test qualification requirements per section 4.3.1
constraints.review_reason: Qualitative qualification requirement; no directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
b. [NCPR 17] Each valve lot shall be qualified by meeting burst pressure test
requirements in accordance with section 4.3.1 in this NASA Technical Specification.
4.3.1 Proof Pressure and Leak Tests

constraints.variable: pneumatic proof pressure
constraints.review_reason: One-sided minimum pressure requirement; lower-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
a. [NCPR 18] All valves shall be proof tested to a minimum pneumatic proof pressure at
1.5xMEOP.

constraints.variable: helium leak test pressure
constraints.review_reason: One-sided minimum test-pressure requirement is not supported. This line also contains an upper-only leak-rate requirement.
constraints.source_text:
b. [NCPR 19] This capability shall be demonstrated on every unit during assembly, with
pressure applied individually to each line and separately to the valve housing through the
actuation ram chamber while the lines are vented.
Included as part of and after every proof pressure test is a helium leak test at a minimum of
1.0xMEOP with a resulting leak rate less than 1x10-6 standard cc/sec.

constraints.variable: resulting leak rate
constraints.review_reason: One-sided upper-bound leak-rate requirement; upper-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
b. [NCPR 19] This capability shall be demonstrated on every unit during assembly, with
pressure applied individually to each line and separately to the valve housing through the
actuation ram chamber while the lines are vented.
Included as part of and after every proof pressure test is a helium leak test at a minimum of
1.0xMEOP with a resulting leak rate less than 1x10-6 standard cc/sec.

constraints.variable: Test coverage: all parent metal shear-sections and all valve parts exposed to pressure after actuation
constraints.review_reason: Qualitative test-coverage requirement; no directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
c. [NCPR 20] The test shall be performed on all parent metal shear-section and all parts
of the valve exposed to pressure after valve actuation (checklist item 7AC).

constraints.variable: All welds: leak testing during assembly or acceptance testing; fracture mechanics and damage tolerance testing satisfy NASA-STD-5019
constraints.review_reason: Qualitative testing and standards-compliance requirements; no directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
d. [NCPR 21] All welds shall be leak tested either during assembly or acceptance testing
(checklist item 32A).
Fracture mechanics and damage tolerance testing are to satisfy NASA-STD-5019.

constraints.variable: Non-destructive acceptance testing or defect-risk mitigation through process control
constraints.review_reason: Alternative qualitative process requirement; no directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
e. [NCPR 22] Either non-destructive acceptance testing (checklist item 6C) shall be
accomplished or the risk of defects be mitigated through process control.

constraints.variable: NASA Fracture Control Board approval when process control is used for applicable spacecraft
constraints.review_reason: Conditional approval requirement; no directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
f. [NCPR 23] If process control is used, approval shall be obtained from the NASA
Fracture Control Board for spacecraft requiring this in programmatic requirements.

constraints.variable: Growth of maximum credible crack size demonstrated to be non-credible
constraints.review_reason: Qualitative fracture-control criterion; no numeric threshold is stated.
constraints.source_text:
g. [NCPR 24] If fracture mechanics and crack growth analysis are used to verify
compliance with NASA-STD-5019 (see section 4.1 of this NASA Technical Specification),
growth of the maximum credible crack size shall be demonstrated to the fracture control
authority to be non-credible, based on knowledge of quality control and manufacturing
techniques used to make the NC parent metal valve.

constraints.variable: NC parent metal valve survival life
constraints.review_reason: One-sided minimum life-multiple requirement; lower-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
h. [NCPR 25] However this capability is technically established, the NC parent metal
valve shall be capable of surviving four times the design operational life.

constraints.variable: proof test pressure independently applied to each parent metal shear-section and externally to the welded shear-section
constraints.review_reason: One-sided minimum proof-pressure requirement is not supported; the no-deformation/leakage criterion is also qualitative.
constraints.source_text:
i. [NCPR 26] If the valve design is to provide two separate and independent parent
metal barriers to the flow before valve actuation, this capability shall be verified by proof testing
at 1.5xMEOP, independently applied to each parent metal shear-section and then externally to

4.3.2 Burst Pressure Test

constraints.variable: hold time for each burst pressure test
constraints.review_reason: One-sided minimum hold-time requirement; lower-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text: a. [NCPR 27] The minimum hold time for each burst pressure test shall be 5 min.

constraints.variable: design burst pressure for lines with diameters ≥3.8 cm (≥1.5 in)
constraints.review_reason: Conditional one-sided minimum pressure requirement; lower-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
b. [NCPR 28] All NC parent metal valves shall meet a minimum design burst pressure
of 2.5xMEOP for lines with diameters ≥3.8 cm (≥1.5 in) or 4.0xMEOP for lines with diameters
<3.8 cm (<1.5 in).

constraints.variable: design burst pressure for lines with diameters <3.8 cm (<1.5 in)
constraints.review_reason: Conditional one-sided minimum pressure requirement; lower-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
b. [NCPR 28] All NC parent metal valves shall meet a minimum design burst pressure
of 2.5xMEOP for lines with diameters ≥3.8 cm (≥1.5 in) or 4.0xMEOP for lines with diameters
<3.8 cm (<1.5 in).

constraints.variable: NC parent metal valves from each lot demonstrated for burst-pressure capability
constraints.review_reason: Minimum sampling-count requirement; count lower-bound constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
(1) [NCPR 29] This capability shall be demonstrated on at least one NC parent metal
valve from each lot.

constraints.variable: minimum design burst pressure for NC parent metal used in hazardous systems without additional barriers to leakage, if required by USAF Range Safety and NASA Payload Safety
constraints.review_reason: Conditional one-sided minimum pressure requirement; lower-bound-only constraint type is not supported.
constraints.source_text:
(2) [NCPR 30] Testing shall be performed before and after actuation and on a sample
of the units that have successfully functioned after destructive acceptance testing
(checklist items 8AD and 33D).
NC parent metal used in hazardous systems without additional barriers to leakage may be
required by USAF Range Safety and NASA Payload Safety to have a minimum design burst
pressure requirement of 4.0 times maximum ground working pressure (MGWP). NC parent
metal valves used in hazardous systems without additional barriers to leakage are considered
Category A ordnance devices and have to follow NASA-STD 8719.24 and AFSPCMAN 91-710,
Volume 3, Chapter 13, or equivalent document for applicable range. This requirement should be
identified and documented early in the launch facility coordination process and be documented
in the tailoring agreement. This requirement would not apply to Category B ordnance pyrovalve
applications, which are, by definition, non-hazardous.
CAUTION:  An expended (fired) pyrovalve may retain significant pressure in the primer
chamber assembly for an indefinite period of time.

constraints.variable: burst-test pressure at which testing can be discontinued if burst has not occurred
constraints.review_reason: Conditional event-based test-discontinuation criterion; not a directly representable supported mathematical constraint.
constraints.source_text:
c. [NCPR 31] If the unit passes the burst pressure test, the pressure shall be increased
until burst actually occurs or 4.00xMEOP is reached, at which point the test can be discontinued.
Additionally, if the valve does not fail after 4.00xMEOP, it meets the full safety factor applied to
tubing <3.81 cm (<1.5in) in diameter (checklist item 33D).
